verified_by: TrueJoyBirthing research (official Florida DOH / Florida Newborn Screening sources)

metabolic_screening.program_name: Florida Newborn Screening Program (Bureau of Public Health Laboratory, Jacksonville)

out_of_hospital_midwife.kit_ordering: Midwives and other out-of-hospital providers order newborn screening cards and mailing supplies via the Florida Newborn Screening Program 'Order Supplies' portal.
out_of_hospital_midwife.submission_deadline: Specimen collected 24+ hours after birth and mailed to the Bureau of Public Health Laboratory in Jacksonville.
out_of_hospital_midwife.specimen_tracking: Results released to the baby's provider; parents advised to ask the baby's doctor for results. Tracking via the Florida Newborn Screening Results (FNSR) system.

metabolic_screening.state_form_note: Florida has NO standalone state opt-out form. Per the program FAQ, while not recommended, parents may refuse newborn screening for any reason; the person responsible for collecting the specimen must obtain a written refusal from the parent and include it in the child's medical record, documenting that the parents were informed of possible adverse outcomes and accept legal responsibility.
metabolic_screening.statute: Florida Statute § 383.04 (eye prophylaxis with written religious objection); newborn screening mandated under Florida Statute Ch. 383 / Ch. 154

hearing_screening.program_name: Florida Early Hearing Detection and Intervention (EHDI)
hearing_screening.out_of_hospital_path: For home/birth-center births, the midwife or birth attendant performs or arranges the newborn hearing screen and documents results; refusal is documented in writing in the medical record per the same refusal policy as metabolic screening.

cchd_screening.out_of_hospital_performer: The attending midwife or birth attendant performs pulse oximetry (CCHD) in the out-of-hospital setting and documents it; refusal documented in writing in the medical record.
cchd_screening.statute: Florida Statute § 383.303 (critical congenital heart defect screening)

erythromycin_eye_ointment.waiver: Parents may submit a written objection stating the medication is contrary to their religious beliefs; provider documents the objection in the medical record.
erythromycin_eye_ointment.note: Attending professional instills an approved prophylactic into the infant's eyes, generally within one hour of birth.

vitamin_k.note: Florida does not mandate vitamin K; parental choice of oral, intramuscular shot, or decline, documented in the birth record.

hepatitis_b_vaccine.birth_dose_registry: Florida SHOTS (State Health Online Tracking System)
hepatitis_b_vaccine.note: Birth dose reported to Florida SHOTS by birthing facilities; infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers are reported to the Florida Department of Health for case management.

gestational_diabetes.midwife_role: Licensed midwives in Florida provide gestational diabetes screening/counseling in prenatal care and refer for diagnostic testing when indicated.
gestational_diabetes.note: Prenatal informed-choice item; no state newborn-screening form.

group_b_strep.midwife_role: Licensed midwives offer GBS screening in late pregnancy and arrange intrapartum prophylaxis per protocol for out-of-hospital births when indicated.
group_b_strep.note: Prenatal informed-choice item; no state newborn-screening form.
